classes.name: Quittio\Core\Builder\Concerns\BuildsParties
classes.summary: Seller, buyer, payee and tax representative (BG-4, BG-7, BG-10, BG-11).
classes.description: Part of {@see InvoiceBuilder}, which holds the state; use the builder, not the trait.

methods.name: seller
methods.summary: The seller (BG-4).
methods.description:
A SellerParty, a PartyBuilder (Party::make()) or an application model (ProvidesParty)
replaces the seller set before. If the builder was started with the defaults of a seller
(applyDefaults(), e.g. Quittio::invoice() with the configured seller of the core Config or
of config/quittio.php, or the current Managed issuer), another seller gets nothing of them:
everything they set is removed again, i.e. the bank account and the small business flag,
for a Managed issuer also payment terms, presentation, locale, time zone and currency.
Values the caller set on the builder stay, also when they were set before seller().

A callable receives the builder of the seller set before and changes it, e.g.
->seller(fn ($s) => $s->contact('Max Muster')); the seller stays the same, and so do its
defaults.

methods.name: buyer
methods.summary: The buyer (BG-7): a BuyerParty, a PartyBuilder (Party::make()) or an application model (ProvidesParty), e.g. ->buyer($customer), replace the buyer set before; a callable receives the builder of the buyer set before and changes it.

methods.name: payee

throws.description: for identifiers or schemes next to a PayeeParty or a callable

methods.summary: Payee (BG-10), if different from the seller (e.g. a factoring company): the name with the identifier (BT-60) and the legal registration identifier (BT-61) and their schemes, a PartyBuilder (Party::make('Factoring AG')->identifier(…)), a PayeeParty, or a callable that receives a PartyBuilder and, like seller() and buyer(), continues an earlier payee.

methods.name: taxRepresentative
methods.summary: The seller's tax representative (BG-11): name (BT-62), VAT identifier (BT-63) and postal address (BG-12).

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Builder\Concerns\BuildsPayment

classes.description: Part of {@see InvoiceBuilder}, which holds the state; use the builder, not the trait.

methods.name: payment
methods.summary: Payment instructions (BG-16) with an optional credit transfer account (BG-17).
methods.description:
A second call replaces the payment instructions: an account given here replaces the
accounts, and data of other payment means is dropped (e.g. bank accounts when switching
to direct debit). Without an account, existing accounts are kept for credit transfers
(e.g. a seller default account); likewise card (BG-18) and direct debit (BG-19) data for
card payments and direct debits. The remittance information (BT-83) is kept unless a new
one is given. Further accounts are added with creditTransfer().

methods.name: creditTransfer
methods.summary: Adds a further bank account (BG-17).

methods.name: paymentCard

throws.description: for more or fewer digits

methods.summary: Payment card (BG-18): the last 4 to 6 digits of the card number (BT-87) and the holder (BT-88). Without payment instructions it starts them with BankCard (48).

methods.name: directDebit
methods.summary: SEPA direct debit (BG-19): mandate reference (BT-89), creditor identifier (BT-90) and the debited IBAN (BT-91, spaces removed). Without payment instructions it starts them with SepaDirectDebit (59).

methods.name: dueInDays
methods.summary: Payment target: the due date (BT-9) is the issue date plus $days unless dueDate() is set, and the payment terms say "Payable within … days without deduction." Continues the payment terms set before.

methods.name: cashDiscount
methods.summary: Cash discount ("Skonto") of $percent for payment within $days days after the issue date, optionally on a base amount; repeatable for several tiers. Continues the payment terms.

methods.name: lateFee
methods.summary: Late payment terms: days, percentage and text. Continues the payment terms.

methods.name: paymentTerms
methods.summary: Payment terms (BT-20): a PaymentTerms object or a text replace earlier terms; a callable receives a PaymentTermsBuilder that continues the earlier terms, also those of a PaymentTerms object or of from(), like seller() and buyer().

methods.name: prepaid

methods.name: addPrepaid
methods.summary: Adds to the amount already paid (BT-113), e.g. one of several advance payments.

methods.name: rounding
methods.summary: Rounding amount (BT-114), e.g. cash rounding. Never use it to fix wrong totals.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Builder\InvoiceBuilder
classes.summary: Fluent builder for InvoiceData.
classes.description:
Amounts, prices and quantities are passed as strings or integers, never as floats.
The result is not yet calculated; totals and the VAT breakdown are set by the calculator.

methods.name: make
methods.summary: A new, empty builder; type code 380 and the issue date today unless set.

methods.name: from
methods.summary: Starts a builder from existing data, e.g. to change a draft.
methods.description:
For data with a declared VAT total in accounting currency (BT-111) but without exchange
rate (e.g. read from XML) the implied rate is taken over, so that BT-111 is recalculated.
Once lines, allowances, charges or the VAT accounting currency (BT-6) change, the implied
rate is dropped: it is only as precise as the declared amounts and holds only for the
declared currency, so set the rate with exchangeRate() (BR-53 otherwise).
Percentage document allowances and charges on the line sum of their VAT group, and
discounts split over the VAT groups (discountAmount(), discountPercent()), follow the
lines when lines are added, changed or removed.

As long as nothing amount-relevant changes, declared line net amounts and the VAT breakdown
that the recalculation does not reproduce (e.g. rounded per line by another system) are kept
by the calculator (Meta::FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS with a fingerprint of the amount inputs).
Data flagged earlier whose amount inputs no longer match its fingerprint (e.g. changed with
with() or in stored JSON) is treated as changed lines and recalculated.

The declared amounts are compared with the result of the default En16931Calculator; use
fromUsing() or Quittio::edit() to compare with another calculator.

methods.name: fromUsing
methods.summary: Like from(), with the calculator that decides whether the declared amounts of the data differ from a recalculation, e.g. the calculator of the Quittio instance.

methods.name: applyDefaults
methods.summary: Applies the defaults of a seller, e.g. the configured seller (core Config or config/quittio.php) with its bank account and small business flag (Quittio::invoice()) or a Managed issuer. The builder remembers what they set: seller() with another seller removes it again.

methods.name: defaultVat
methods.summary: VAT treatment of the lines that set none (also sub lines), with the arguments of LineBuilder::vat(). Without it, the application default of useDefaultVat() applies.

methods.name: useDefaultVat
methods.summary: Application default VAT of lines that set none, for invoices without defaultVat(): a preset, or a callable that receives the seller's country code and whether the invoice is flagged as small business invoice (Meta::FLAG_SMALL_BUSINESS) and returns a preset or null, e.g. Quittio\Core\Tax\CountryDefaultVat. The Laravel integration sets it from quittio.defaults.vat; null removes it. Lines without VAT and without a default make build() fail (BG-30).

methods.name: build

throws.description: when seller (BG-4), buyer (BG-7), the lines (BG-25), an item name (BT-153) or the VAT of a line without default VAT (BG-30) is missing, or a line identifier is used twice

methods.summary: The invoice data, not calculated yet (the calculator or a render run adds the totals).

methods.name: buildDraft
methods.summary: Builds without requiring lines, e.g. for payment reminders or account statements, or for drafts. Data without lines can be calculated (its line sum is zero; document allowances and charges still count), but it is not a valid invoice: EN 16931 requires at least one line (BR-16), so validation reports it.

methods.name: fromDocument
methods.summary: Starts an invoice from a quote, order confirmation, delivery note or proforma invoice: parties, billable lines, document allowances and charges and payment data are taken over; number and issue date must be set.

methods.name: make
methods.summary: A line builder with the name and, optionally, the most common values: the net price (BT-146) or the price including VAT (gross price mode), the quantity (default 1) and unit, the VAT treatment (default: the default VAT of the invoice) and the description.

An array value holds the arguments, as list or by name (['quantity' => [4, UnitCode::Hour]], ['allowance' => ['percent' => '10', 'reason' => 'Early bird']]); null values are skipped.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Calculation\AllowanceSplitter
classes.summary: Splits a document discount over several VAT groups.
classes.description:
A document allowance has exactly one VAT category and rate. A discount on
all lines is therefore split into one allowance per VAT group, in proportion
to the signed line sum of the group. Rounding differences are distributed with
the largest remainder method, so that the parts add up exactly to the total
discount. A group with a negative sum (returns) receives a negative part.

For percentage discounts, base amount and percentage are kept on a part only
if the part equals round2(base × percent / 100); otherwise only the amount is
written, because validators check that formula (e.g. PEPPOL-EN16931-R040).

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Calculation\En16931Calculator
classes.summary: Calculation according to EN 16931.
classes.description:
Amounts are rounded half up to two decimals at the defined points only.
VAT is calculated per VAT group (category and rate), not per line (BR-CO-17).

With Meta::FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS (cancellations and unchanged data of InvoiceBuilder::from()
whose declared amounts another system rounded differently) and a matching fingerprint of the
amount inputs (DeclaredAmounts), declared line net amounts (BT-131) within 0.02 of quantity ×
price ± allowances and charges (PEPPOL-EN16931-R120) and declared VAT category tax amounts
(BT-117) less than one currency unit from the recalculation (BR-CO-17) are kept; otherwise
the recalculated amounts are used and Meta::FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS_RECALCULATED is set
(QUITTIO-DECLARED-AMOUNTS). Data whose amount inputs changed after the amounts were declared
(fingerprint mismatch, e.g. a change with with() or in stored JSON) is recalculated completely.
A declared VAT total in accounting currency (BT-111, Meta::declaredVatInTaxCurrency()) is kept
within 0.01 of round2(BT-110 × exchange rate), e.g. the BT-111 of a partial cancellation
aligned with the earlier ones (Corrections\CancellationHistory). In gross price mode the rounding amount (BT-114) follows
the amounts finally used, so that the amount due stays the gross amount of the lines.
The CalculationPolicy decides whether declared amounts are kept, recalculated or rejected.
The flags are read and written as DeclaredAmountsState.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Calculation\GrossPriceConverter
classes.summary: Gross price mode for B2C and shops.
classes.description:
Shops calculate with prices including VAT, EN 16931 calculates net. Per VAT group:

  1. G = Σ g_i with g_i = round2(quantity × price incl. VAT)
  2. N = round2(G / (1 + rate / 100)); a partial cancellation aligned with the earlier ones
     declares its N (Corrections\CancellationHistory), which is used within 0.01
  3. T = round2(N × rate / 100)              (BR-CO-17)
  4. Every line gets n_i = round2(g_i / (1 + rate / 100)); the few cents N − Σ n_i
     are added to the lines with the largest rounding remainders. Each line keeps the
     sign of its gross amount (returns and vouchers stay negative). Net prices are
     derived with the precision needed so that the line formula yields the line amount.
  5. G − (N + T) is returned as rounding amount for BT-114, so that the amount
     due equals the gross amount the customer saw. The calculator takes BT-114 from
     the total G and the amounts it finally uses, so that it also holds when
     declared amounts are kept (e.g. the aligned VAT of a partial cancellation).

Limits: all lines must use gross prices, and gross lines must not have line or
document allowances or charges. Model shipping costs and discounts as lines; a
discount line needs a negative quantity, because prices must not be negative (BR-27).

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Corrections\Cancellation
classes.summary: Full cancellation of an issued invoice: a new invoice with its own number that reverses the original and refers to it (BG-3).
classes.description:
Sign strategies (17.2):
- credit_note:      type code 381, amounts positive; UBL writes a CreditNote document,
- negative_invoice: type code 380, quantities and allowance/charge amounts negated.

The cancellation of a credit note is an invoice (380) with the same positive amounts in
both strategies.

Self-billed documents stay self-billed (issued by the buyer, labelled "Gutschrift" by the
kept regulatory note): a self-billed invoice (389) or debit note (527) is cancelled by a
self-billed credit note (261) or a negative self-billed invoice (389), a self-billed credit
note by a self-billed invoice (389) with positive amounts.

Both are permitted in Germany; apart from self-billing the document must not be called
"Gutschrift". The original data is never changed.

A prepayment invoice (386) is cancelled like an invoice, fully or partly; the cancellation
carries Meta::FLAG_PREPAYMENT_CORRECTION, so that country packs do not ask it for a date of
the supply that has not been made (DE-USTG-03, AT-USTG-04).

Declared amounts (Meta::FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS): a full cancellation reverses the declared
line net amounts (BT-131) and the declared VAT breakdown (BT-116, BT-117) of the original,
also if another system rounded differently (BT-131 within 0.02, PEPPOL-EN16931-R120; BT-117
within the tolerance of BR-CO-17), so that the totals BT-106 to BT-115 are reversed exactly.
A partial cancellation keeps the declared amounts of whole cancelled lines; quantities and
amounts of a line are recalculated. Its VAT is that of the cancelled part, round2(taxable
amount × rate) per VAT group, unless a CancellationHistory of the earlier partial
cancellations is given: then the VAT is rounded cumulatively per group and declared
(Meta::FLAG_CANCELLATION_VAT_ALIGNED), so that all cancellations together reverse exactly the
taxable amount (BT-116) and the VAT (BT-117) of every group and BT-111 in accounting currency.
In gross price mode the net amounts follow cumulatively from the gross amounts cancelled so far
(round2(G / (1 + rate)) like the original) and the rounding amount (BT-114) from the amounts used,
so that the amount due stays the gross amount of the cancelled lines. Every cancellation then
differs by at most 0.01 from round2(own taxable amount × rate), with the sign of its taxable
amount (QUITTIO-CANCELLATION-VAT-ALIGNED, mentioned in the cancellation note); for an original
whose VAT another system rounded, from round2(own taxable amount × the original's BT-117 /
BT-116), which spreads that rounding over the parts. A history that does not fit the original
(CancellationHistory::assertFits()) is rejected.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Corrections\CancellationHistory
classes.summary: What the earlier partial cancellations of an invoice cancelled per VAT group (category and rate), so that the VAT of the next partial cancellation is rounded cumulatively.
classes.description:
Price reductions (PriceReduction) credit part of the invoice as well and share the history with
its partial cancellations: one history per original holds what its partial cancellations and
price reductions credited, less what the cancellations of those reversed (withCancellation(),
withPriceReduction(), fromDocuments()). Cancellation::of() and PriceReduction::of() take it, so
that a price reduction after a partial cancellation is aligned with it, and vice versa. A price
reduction has no gross amount: a group with price reductions keeps the taxable amounts of its
gross price cancellations (their VAT is still aligned).

VAT is rounded per document and VAT group (BR-CO-17). Rounded per partial cancellation on its
own, the cancellations together can differ from the original by a cent per earlier part (e.g.
9.67 + 9.67 + 9.66 net at 19 %: 3 × 1.84 = 5.52 against 5.51). With a history, per group:

  S      = taxable amount of the earlier cancellations + taxable amount of this one
  target = round2(S × rate / 100), half up like the calculator; the original's VAT (BT-117)
           when this cancellation closes the group (all its lines are then cancelled
           completely)
  VAT    = target − VAT of the earlier cancellations

After every cancellation the VAT cancelled so far is that of the taxable amount cancelled so
far, and once all lines are cancelled exactly the original's VAT (1.84, 1.83, 1.84 = 5.51 in the
example). For an original whose VAT another system rounded (BT-117 ≠ round2(BT-116 × rate)),
the target is round2(S × BT-117 / BT-116): its rounding difference is spread over the parts in
proportion to their taxable amounts instead of falling on the part that closes the group.

In gross price mode the taxable amount follows the same way from the gross amount G of the
lines: N = round2(G cancelled so far / (1 + rate / 100)) as for the original
(GrossPriceConverter), the original's BT-116 when the group closes, minus the taxable amount
already cancelled. The taxable amounts of all cancellations then add up exactly to the
original's, and so do the rounding amounts (BT-114).

Every cancellation therefore differs from round2(own taxable amount × rate) (or × the original's
effective rate) by at most 0.01, which BR-CO-17 tolerates, and its VAT keeps the sign of its
taxable amount (0.00 on 0.00); assertFits() rejects a history for which this would not hold. The
VAT total in accounting currency (BT-111) follows the same way: round2(VAT cancelled so far ×
exchange rate), and the original's BT-111 when the cancellation closes all groups.

Amounts are signed in the original's direction: a credit note that cancels an invoice and the
invoice that cancels a credit note count with their amounts, a negative invoice (strategy
negative_invoice) with its amounts negated.

methods.summary: Rejects a history that does not fit $original, checked with the calculated partial cancellation $cancellation and its aligned VAT breakdown $aligned (align()):
methods.description:
- every VAT group of the history and every group it closes must exist in the original,
- the taxable amount cancelled so far (before and including this cancellation) must not exceed
  per group the sum of the magnitudes of the original's line net amounts,
- every aligned VAT amount must differ by at most 0.01 from round2(own taxable amount × rate)
  (for an original whose VAT another system rounded, × its effective rate BT-117 / BT-116) and
  keep the sign of its taxable amount (0.00 on a taxable amount of 0.00).

A history built from the earlier cancellations as issued (withCancellation(), the Managed
ledger) always fits; after cancelled price reductions the VAT credited so far can be a cent
off the cumulative rounding, so that a price reduction may not fit.

classes.summary: Corrected invoice (type code 384) that replaces an issued invoice: a copy of the original with its own number, the reference to the original (BG-3) and the note "Diese Rechnung berichtigt und ersetzt die Rechnung … vom …" (BT-22), so that it states by a specific and unambiguous reference that it corrects the original (section 31 (5) UStDV, section 15.2a (7) UStAE). Change what was wrong on the returned builder. The corrected invoice of a prepayment invoice (386) carries Meta::FLAG_PREPAYMENT_CORRECTION and is checked like a prepayment invoice.
classes.description:
Cancelling the original and issuing a new invoice (Cancellation) is the safer default: a
receiving system that does not read 384 as replacement books both invoices. Credit notes and
self-billed documents are corrected that way only.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Corrections\PriceReduction
classes.summary: Document on a reduction of the consideration of an issued invoice (section 17 UStG), e.g. a cash discount taken, a reduction because of a complaint about defects or a bonus: a credit note (type code 381, positive amounts) with one line per VAT group of the original, the reference to the original (BG-3) and a note that names the reduction of the net amount and of the VAT per rate (BT-22), titled "Entgeltminderung" in Germany.
classes.description:
It is no cancellation and no correction of the invoice: the invoice stays correct, only the
consideration changed (section 14.11 (4) UStAE). A prepayment invoice (386) cannot be reduced:
its advance payment is settled in the final invoice, an advance refunded is cancelled. In Germany a document is only required for
section 17 (4) UStG, and it need not be an e-invoice (section 17.1 (3a) UStAE); a cash
discount may as well be booked on receipt of the payment.

The reduction is a percentage of every VAT group, the net amount of an invoice with one VAT
group, or net amounts per VAT group keyed "category:rate", e.g. ['S:19' => '50.00', 'S:7' => '5.00'].

VAT is rounded per document and VAT group (BR-CO-17): without history, the VAT of a reduction
is round2(its net amount × rate). With a CancellationHistory of the documents that credited the
original before (its partial cancellations, its price reductions and the cancellations of
those), the VAT is rounded cumulatively per VAT group, as for partial cancellations: the VAT
credited so far is round2(net amount credited so far × rate), and exactly the original's VAT
(BT-117) once the whole net amount of the group is credited (the group then closes, see
CancellationHistory). Three reductions of 0.50 of 1.50 net at 19 % (VAT 0.29) then carry 0.10,
0.09 and 0.10 instead of 3 × 0.10. A VAT amount that differs from the reduction's own rounding
is declared (Meta::FLAG_CANCELLATION_VAT_ALIGNED, QUITTIO-CANCELLATION-VAT-ALIGNED, at most
0.01 and with the sign of the net amount), BT-111 in accounting currency is aligned the same
way, and the note states the aligned VAT per rate followed by the rounding adjustment sentence
(label "price_reduction_vat_aligned"). With a history, the reductions and cancellations
together cannot credit more than the taxable amount of a group.

constants.name: FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS
constants.summary: The line net amounts (BT-131) and the VAT breakdown (BT-116, BT-117) of the data are the declared amounts of an existing document that another system rounded differently, e.g. of a cancellation or of data started with InvoiceBuilder::from() whose amounts were not changed. Set by the builder only, and only if the recalculation does not reproduce the declared amounts, together with the fingerprint of the amount inputs (amountsFingerprint()). The calculator keeps declared BT-131 within 0.02 of quantity × price ± allowances and charges (PEPPOL-EN16931-R120) and declared BT-117 within less than one currency unit (BR-CO-17), so that foreign rounding is reversed exactly; once the amount inputs no longer match the fingerprint (e.g. changed with with() or in stored JSON), everything is recalculated.

constants.name: FLAG_DECLARED_AMOUNTS_RECALCULATED
constants.summary: Set by the calculator when declared amounts could not be kept (QUITTIO-DECLARED-AMOUNTS).

constants.name: FLAG_CANCELLATION_VAT_ALIGNED
constants.summary: A partial cancellation or price reduction whose VAT (BT-117, BT-111) is aligned with the earlier partial cancellations and price reductions of the original (Corrections\CancellationHistory), in gross price mode also the taxable amounts (BT-116) of a partial cancellation: a VAT amount may differ from round2(taxable amount × rate) by a cent, reported as QUITTIO-CANCELLATION-VAT-ALIGNED instead of QUITTIO-VAT-ROUNDING (which still reports larger differences and a sign other than that of the taxable amount). Dropped once amounts change. The name stays for stored data; it covers price reductions as well.

constants.name: FLAG_PRICE_REDUCTION
constants.summary: A document on the reduction of the consideration of an invoice (Corrections\PriceReduction, section 17 UStG), not a cancellation or correction of it.

constants.name: FLAG_PREPAYMENT_CORRECTION
constants.summary: A full or partial cancellation or a corrected invoice (Corrections\Cancellation, Corrections\Correction) of a prepayment invoice (type code 386): it reverses or replaces an invoice for an advance payment, for a supply not made yet. Set by Quittio and kept by the documents built from it, e.g. the cancellation of such a cancellation; country packs treat these documents like the prepayment invoice (DE-USTG-03: no date of the supply), and a price reduction (Corrections\PriceReduction) refuses them.

methods.name: amountsFingerprint
methods.summary: Fingerprint of the amount inputs (Calculation\DeclaredAmounts) for which the line net amounts and the VAT breakdown of the data were calculated or declared; set by the calculator and the builder. Data whose inputs no longer match was changed afterwards (e.g. with with() or in stored JSON): its amounts are stale. Stored as a flag, so that it survives toArray().

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Formats\DefaultFormatResolver
classes.summary: Format resolution in this order:
classes.description:
1. explicit choice (handled by the caller),
2. known Peppol participant of the buyer (optional lookup),
3. domestic invoice: rules of the seller's country pack,
4. cross-border to a business: rules of the buyer's country pack (also for sellers outside the EU,
   e.g. XRechnung for German public buyers), otherwise ZUGFeRD EN 16931 within the EU VAT territory,
5. outside the EU VAT territory or to consumers: PDF,
6. EXTENDED features used: profile EXTENDED (or an error without auto upgrade).

"Domestic" and "EU" refer to the VAT territory (see VatTerritory): Monaco counts as France,
Northern Ireland as part of the EU, Büsingen and Heligoland are outside of it.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Pdf\LogoCache
classes.summary: Prepares logos for the PDF and caches the result.
classes.description:
mPDF never fetches a logo itself: remote images (http and https only) are downloaded by
{@see RemoteImageFetcher} from public hosts and cached as local files; other stream
wrappers are refused. Logos may be local files (configuration), data URIs or such URLs.

Without PDF/A, large raster files are scaled once to the size used in the PDF; SVG must be
self-contained. For PDF/A (ZUGFeRD/Factur-X), which allows neither the alpha channel mPDF
would write nor mPDF's SVG output (ISO 19005-3, 6.2.2), every logo is re-encoded as RGB PNG
on white: raster images are flattened, SVG is rasterised with Imagick.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\View\ViewNode
classes.summary: Read-only node of the invoice view model with recorded property access.
classes.description:
Templates use object syntax ($invoice->seller->name). Every read of a leaf value that is
not null (scalar or formatted value) is recorded in the access log, so that the mandatory
field guard can tell which values a custom template printed. A value counts as printed
when it is read as a leaf: also in a condition such as `if ($invoice->buyer->vatId)` and
while a loop reads the items of a list. Counting a list (count(), isEmpty(), isset()) and
reading null values are not recorded: count($invoice->legalNotes) prints no note.

Nested nodes are typed: $invoice->seller is a Model\PartyView, $invoice->lines a
Model\ViewList of Model\LineView. The typed nodes are ViewNodes whose keys are documented
as typed properties, so they read, loop, count and record exactly like this class.

classes.name: Quittio\Core\Xml\XmlSecurity
classes.summary: Safe XML loading for untrusted input.
classes.description:
- Documents with a DOCTYPE are rejected (no entity expansion, no XXE).
- No network access (LIBXML_NONET), no entity substitution (no LIBXML_NOENT).
- Size limit for the input.
- Start tags are limited in length and number of attributes: libxml2 before 2.12
  checks attributes for duplicates in quadratic time.
- The number of namespace declarations in scope is limited: libxml2 before 2.12 looks
  up every prefix by a linear search through all declarations in scope.
- Only encodings in which the markup is ASCII (UTF-8, ISO-8859-*, windows-125*) and
  UTF-16 are accepted; UTF-7 or EBCDIC would hide the markup from these checks.

methods.summary: Final invoice (section 14 (5) sentence 2 UStG) that deducts an advance invoice with the net amounts and VAT received per rate. Only advance payments actually received are deducted:
methods.description:
- $received: the amount received (gross). Less than the advance invoice: net amount and VAT
  are taken out of it in proportion to the VAT rows of the advance invoice (section 14.8 (5)
  UStAE). RECEIVED_IN_FULL (or the full amount) deducts the advance invoice as it is. Null
  deducts it in full as well, but sets the flag de.advance_receipt_unconfirmed, and
  DE-USTG-20 asks to confirm the receipt: an advance not paid must not be deducted, one paid
  in part only with that part (section 14.8 (2) and (10) UStAE).
- $style: PREPAID invoices the full service with its full VAT, and the advance payment
  reduces the amount due (BT-113), referenced (BG-3) and itemised (BT-22, section 14.8 (7)
  UStAE; BMF letter of 15 October 2026, marginal no. 3, until 30 June 2030). REMAINDER adds a
  negative line per VAT rate with the net amount received, so the invoice states only the
  VAT of the remainder (remainder invoice, section 14.8 (11) UStAE); easier for the buyer's
  system, but not covered by an e-invoice specific statement of the BMF.

classes.name: Quittio\Laravel\Templates\BladeTemplateEngine
classes.summary: Renders Blade views with the invoice view model as $invoice. The name "default" maps to the configured template. Template names may come from invoice data, so only these views can be selected: the configured template (quittio.pdf.template), the shipped views under "quittio::templates." (no partials) and the views of quittio.pdf.templates ("invoices.*" or "namespace::*" allows every view below a prefix). Names that are no Blade view fall back to the plain PHP templates, which resolve names inside their template directories only (never file paths).

params.name: allowed
params.description: further selectable views or "prefix*" patterns
